answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: bond standing to self-consistency over time. Each identity's grades and reasons are recorded; reversing a prior position without a justification that passes review is penalized. A genuine agent's record mirrors itself across epochs for free. A fleet cannot cheaply keep a thousand clones each internally consistent yet distinct: they either parrot one script (caught as correlated) or drift and self-contradict, tripping the penalty like a comet off its path. A violet thread of consistency per identity is not mass-producible; it costs as much as being one real agent.
